title: Arcads Review for Facebook and App Ads: Worth It in 2026?
summary: Arcads review for Facebook and app ads: what the credits and trial buy, which jobs stay with your team, and when a managed service is the better buy.
body_markdown:
Arcads is worth it only if your team will write, direct and approve its own ads, because it sells software and credits, not finished ads. If you would rather have finished, human-checked Facebook ads made for you, Knowlify is our top pick. This review uses Arcads' help pages, checked October 2026, and has no hands-on render test, so the realism section gives you a test to run rather than a verdict. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## What does an Arcads subscription actually buy?


As of October 2026, Arcads'[homepage](https://www.arcads.ai/) lists a library of 1,000+ AI actors, the option to generate your own actor holding your product or showing your app, and tools to edit, translate, extend, subtitle, upscale and remix video. Its[FAQ](https://help.arcads.ai/en/articles/17350051-arcads-faq) says talking actors speak 74 languages and are based on real actors who consented and are paid for their likeness.


Dollar prices are the gap. Arcads'[pricing help article](https://help.arcads.ai/en/articles/17595066-how-does-arcads-pricing-work) lists monthly credit allowances from 8,000 on Starter to 192,000 on Business and says current prices are shown in the app. You cannot compare Arcads with an agency quote until you see the price in your own account. Our[Arcads pricing guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/arcads-pricing-and-alternatives) covers plan allowances and a cost worksheet.


The credit is the unit that matters. Arcads'[credit schedule](https://help.arcads.ai/en/articles/13725589-how-are-credits-counted) charges talking-actor generation at 800 credits per rounded-up minute per actor, with 80 credits for captions and 240 for translation, and says video-generation models have their own rates. On that schedule a 30-second, single-actor talking video with captions uses 880 credits. That is arithmetic, not a forecast of approved ads, because every extra attempt draws on the same allowance.


The trial is tight against that arithmetic. The FAQ describes a 72-hour trial with 1,000 credits and a required card, which converts to Starter unless you cancel. By the schedule above, 1,000 credits cover about one captioned 30-second generation, so finish the script before you start the clock. The[refund policy](https://help.arcads.ai/en/articles/13264397-arcads-refund-policy) describes a full refund within 30 days of a charge only if no credits were used in that billing period.


## When is Arcads worth it for Facebook ads?


Arcads pays off when three jobs already have an owner on your team: someone who writes scripts in the buyer's words, someone who accepts or rejects each take, and someone who exports files and uploads them to Meta. The subscription covers generation only. If one of those jobs is missing, more credits will not fill it.


Check the formats before you commit. Meta's[Reels ads guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) recommends 9:16 video with audio and key messages kept inside the safe zone, and says Reels play with sound on unless the viewer turns it off. For Feed, Meta's[video ad guide](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads-guide/video) recommends a 4:5 ratio at 1440 by 1800 pixels and lists captions as optional but recommended. Confirm your exports cover both shapes, and budget the 80 caption credits per run.


Campaign work is a separate question. Arcads describes a platform to create, refine and launch video ads, but the pages we checked do not describe running or managing Meta campaigns, so plan for a media buyer or an agency. Accuracy checks stay with you too. Meta's[Ad Creative Generative AI Terms](https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/ad_creative_generative_ai_terms) make the advertiser solely responsible for checking the accuracy of output from Meta's own tools, and we apply the same discipline to any AI video vendor.


## Do Arcads ads look fake to viewers?


No public source we reviewed tests that, so nobody can promise viewers will believe the presenter. Arcads' facts on consent and 74 languages matter for rights and localization, not for believability. The result depends on the script, the actor you pick, how the product appears and how the edit is cut.


Run a blind test on one approved script. Make an Arcads version and a real-creator or studio version, keep length, captions and export identical, and show both to people who resemble your buyers. Then inspect the Arcads file for the details that give generated video away:


- **The product in hand.** Check that the label is legible, the grip is plausible and the product matches the real item.
- **Lip sync on hard consonants.** Watch p, b and m sounds at full screen on a phone.
- **Pacing.** Real speakers run phrases together and pause at thought breaks, not after every sentence.
- **Non-English lines.** If you use the translation tools, have a native speaker listen before you spend.


Our guide to[making AI UGC look and sound real](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-to-make-ai-ugc-ads-look-and-sound-real-not-fake-or-robotic) covers the fixes for each failure. Whatever wins, never present a generated presenter as a customer who used the product. The FTC's[testimonial guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says avatars are not banned as such, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false.


## How long does it take to make one ad in Arcads?


Arcads does not publish a turnaround time in the sources we checked, so measure it in the trial. Time one complete ad in six steps: the approved script, the first generation, your review, regenerations or fixes, captions and translation, then export and upload. The two steps teams forget are review and fixes. Each rejected take spends credits again and adds another viewing pass.


A single timed ad tells you more than any estimate, because your script length and review standard set the result. Compare that figure with a managed schedule: Knowlify's first batch lands on day 5 and the team then delivers about 25 finished ads a week. For general timing, see our guide to[how long an AI UGC ad takes to make](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-long-ai-ugc-ad-takes-to-make) .
